newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up as corruption scam woes ease.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up as corruption scam woes ease.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended firmer Friday, although in volatile trade, as worries eased over an alleged vote-buying scam involving a re-election bill, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks rose 145 points, or 1.4 percent, to close at 10,499 points. Market volume totalled 576.4 million reais ($543.7 million).
Brokers said market sentiment improved considerably as local newspapers today did not bring any fresh corruption allegations involving a key government minister.
"The market was much calmer today. There were no rumors," said a senior trader.

Brazil's stock market was rattled this week by reports by Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper alleging that deputies took bribes to vote in favor of a bill allowing Brazil's president, governors and mayors to run for a second consecutive term.
It also alleged that Communications Minister Sergio Motta may have provided some of the money paid to the deputies. Motta has strongly denied any role in the scandal.
The reports were based on tapes of conversations Folha claims it had obtained in which a lawmaker suggests he and four other deputies received cash in exchange for their votes.
Despite today's rise, traders said the market's behavior next week would depend on any further news published in local papers and magazines over the weekend.
"If nothing new emerges, the market will resume its uptrend," another trader said.
Telecommunications stocks led the bolsa's rally. Bellwether Telebras gained 2.15 percent, ending the week at 132.80 reais.
Among other blue-chips, traders noted state oil firm climbing 4.32 percent to close at 240.99 reais.
Private CVRD, which had been losing ground since a group led by CSN bought control of the firm, rose 1.26 percent to 24.20 reais.

The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index .IEE, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, fell 1.44 percent to 2,733 points, with federal power utility Eletrobras losing 0.98 percent to 507 reais.
